entry.title: production-old-DO-NOT-DELETE
entry.summary: Dima deletes a database and finds out, too late, which one was the real one.

entry.title: Claude & Dima
entry.summary: 29 short comedy episodes about a developer, Dima, and Claude, the AI that works with him: limits, prompts, deleted databases and dates. Each about a minute, with the full script.

entry.title: 提示词的逻辑与生活：21个要素，7类推理
entry.summary: 写好提示词，用的就是日常生活中清晰思考的那套逻辑：前提、范围、定义、约束、目标、证据和检验。本页面向所有人讲解提示词的21个要素，还有一个实时提示词构建器和一个小游戏。

entry.title: Логика промпта и жизни — 21 часть, 7 видов рассуждения
entry.summary: Хороший промпт строится на той же логике, что и ясное мышление в жизни: посылки, рамки, определения, ограничения, цель, свидетельства и проверка. Двадцать одна часть промпта простыми словами, живой конструктор промптов и игра.

entry.title: プロンプトの論理と人生 — 21の要素、7種類の推論
entry.summary: よいプロンプトを書くときに使うのは、日々の生活ではっきり考えるときと同じ論理です。前提、範囲、定義、制約、ゴール、根拠、検証。プロンプトの21の要素を誰にでもわかるように説明し、その場で試せるプロンプト作成ツールとゲームも用意しました。

entry.title: La lógica de un prompt y de la vida — 21 partes, 7 tipos de razonamiento
entry.summary: Escribir un buen prompt usa la misma lógica que pensar con claridad en la vida diaria: premisas, alcance, definiciones, restricciones, una meta, evidencia y pruebas. Veintiuna partes de un prompt, explicadas para todo el mundo, con un constructor de prompts en vivo y un juego.

entry.title: The Logic of a Prompt & Life — 21 parts, 7 kinds of reasoning
entry.summary: Writing a good prompt uses the same logic as clear thinking in everyday life: premises, scope, definitions, constraints, a goal, evidence and tests. Twenty-one parts of a prompt, explained for everyone, with a live prompt builder and a game.

entry.title: SWARM — STARLINK, ONEWEB & THE MEGACONSTELLATIONS
entry.summary: An interactive field guide to satellite megaconstellations: Iridium, Globalstar and Teledesic in the 1990s, Starlink's shells and laser links, OneWeb, Amazon Leo and China's Guowang and Qianfan; how many satellites continuous coverage really needs, why low orbits beat geostationary ones and even fibre on latency, how satellite streaks land on a telescope image, and how often Starlink dodges collisions — with counts dated October 2026.

entry.title: RELAY — TELSTAR, SYNCOM & THE GEOSTATIONARY IDEA
entry.summary: An interactive field guide to communications satellites: Potočnik's and Clarke's orbit that keeps pace with the turning Earth, Echo 1's 30-metre balloon, Telstar's 12-to-44-minute passes over Andover and the radiation that killed it, Syncom 2's figure eight and Syncom 3's Tokyo Olympics, Early Bird, the Soviet Molniya orbit at 63.4°, and the crowded geostationary belt of today, with its 0.24-second delay.

entry.title: PASSENGER — LAIKA, BELKA & STRELKA, HAM AND THE BIOLOGY FLIGHTS
entry.summary: An interactive field guide to the animals that flew before people: V-2 fruit flies and the Albert monkeys, Dezik and Tsygan, Laika's overheating cabin on Sputnik 2, Belka and Strelka's first return from orbit, Ham's 14.6 g overshoot on Mercury-Redstone 2, Enos, Félicette, the Zond 5 tortoises and the Bion biosatellites — what each flight proved for Gagarin and Shepard, what it could not, and the animals who died.

entry.title: FORECAST — TIROS, GOES, METEOSAT & WEATHER FROM ORBIT
entry.summary: An interactive field guide to weather satellites: TIROS-1's first cloud picture in 1960, Nimbus and the Soviet Meteor system, ATS-1's spin-scan camera and the first full-disk image, GOES and Meteosat, today's GOES-19, Meteosat Third Generation, Himawari and Fengyun; how often geostationary and polar orbiters look at each latitude, why a 2 km pixel grows to 6 km at 60° north, and how Planck's law turns a cloud top's infrared glow into its temperature and height.

entry.title: BUCKET — CORONA, ZENIT & THE FIRST SPY SATELLITES
entry.summary: An interactive field guide to the first photo-reconnaissance satellites: the U-2 gap, twelve failed Discoverer launches before a film capsule was caught in mid-air over the Pacific on 19 August 1960, the CORONA panoramic cameras from KH-1 (12 m) to KH-4B (1.8 m), the Soviet Zenit that brought its whole camera home in a Vostok-type capsule, the turn to digital imaging in 1976, and the 1995 declassification that put 860,000 Cold War photographs to work in archaeology and glaciology.

entry.title: Planck to Horizon — every size in nature
entry.summary: A continuous zoom through 62 steps of ten, from the Planck length to the observable universe, with a mass–size map of everything in between. 175 sourced objects, where sizes meet, where a human stands, and what physics rules at each scale.

entry.title: Rind — Video Synths
entry.summary: Flatten the Earth sixteen ways, move the centre anywhere, and drag the land through the stretch. Map projections on one black wall with a globe beside them: Tissot circles, area and angle heat maps, lines of no distortion, great circles and rhumb lines, carry a country to the equator. WebGL 2 instrument.

entry.title: Relic — Video Synths
entry.summary: The oldest light in the universe, as Planck mapped it: the real SMICA all-sky map of the cosmic microwave background, rendered on the GPU from its HEALPix pixels. Switch on our own motion and watch the dipole swamp everything; blur it to COBE's 7° beam; read the statistics of the actual map; hear its power spectrum as a chord.

entry.title: Re-entry — Video Synths
entry.summary: A capsule's heat shield in the plasma it makes, driven by a real entry simulation: speed, altitude and deceleration integrated step by step, stagnation heating from Sutton–Graves, the shield's glow from its radiative-equilibrium temperature, the shock wave from Billig's correlation. Apollo 11, Stardust, Apollo 7. WebGL 2 study with sound.

entry.title: Plume — Video Synths
entry.summary: A rocket exhaust with its shock diamonds, computed from the nozzle's area ratio and the air pressure at each altitude: over-expanded at sea level, ideal at the design altitude, ballooning in near vacuum. Isentropic flow, US Standard Atmosphere 1976, Prandtl–Meyer expansion. WebGL 2 study with sound.

entry.title: Orbit Loom — Video Synths
entry.summary: A sun-synchronous satellite weaves its ground track over the Earth, one thread per orbit, crossing the equator at the same local time every time, until the pattern repeats. J2 orbital mechanics, a repeat-orbit solver checked against Landsat and Sentinel-2, live swath coverage. WebGL 2 data sculpture with sound.

entry.title: Light-Day — Video Synths
entry.summary: A radio pulse leaves Earth every hour and travels to Voyager 1 at the speed of light, drawn in true proportion. On 18 November 2026 Voyager 1 is one light-day from Earth. Light time solved from JPL Horizons ephemerides; WebGL 2 data sculpture.

entry.title: Chirp — Video Synths
entry.summary: Two black holes spiral together and space carries their gravitational waves outward as tightening spiral lines. Built on LIGO's open data for GW150914 and its numerical-relativity waveform; play the real chirp, compare the simple formula with the data, try your own masses. WebGL 2 data sculpture with sound.

entry.title: Upside Down — Video Synths
entry.summary: A fan of light beams falls onto a water surface and continues below it: refracted into the water and mirrored by a surface you can ripple with your hand. Each beam is a voice, detuned by the waves. WebGL 2 instrument.

entry.title: Threshold — Video Synths
entry.summary: A field of grain with moving contour bands: paint pressure with the pointer, trigger accumulate, saturate and release events, and hear a drone shaped by the same numbers. Black, grey and red. WebGL 2 instrument.

entry.title: Sensor — Video Synths
entry.summary: Forty-eight strata of fine lines bent by a data stream you do not see: a tide model, a machine log, your typing rhythm or your hand. Hover to reveal the raw signal; turn on sound to hear the strata. WebGL 2 instrument.

entry.title: Ring — Video Synths
entry.summary: One laser circle drawn over and over in haze, leaving a fading trace on a photosensitive wall; rings tilt slowly in space, and sound (internal or your microphone) holds them together or breaks them into fragments. WebGL 2 study.

entry.title: Erosion — Video Synths
entry.summary: A real photogrammetry scan of a city block as 225,000 points, kept with its flaws, slowly falling apart: release fronts move through it, points drop, pool like liquid at the ground, and the block rebuilds. WebGL 2 study.

entry.title: Cone — Video Synths
entry.summary: Laser beams on rotating mounts sweep cones, cylinders and fans through a hazy black room. Red light, one white key beam, grain, and slow phases from calm to intense. Volumetric WebGL 2 study with optional sound.

entry.title: Chain — Video Synths
entry.summary: Build a video-feedback effect from passes you can see: transform, blur, displace, melt, threshold, edge, kaleidoscope, mirror, hue and fade. Reorder them, read what each one does and its shader line, and paint into the loop. WebGL 2 instrument.

entry.title: Flock — Video Synths
entry.summary: Reynolds' boids in 3D: a flock of starlings or a school of sardines that forms from three local rules (separation, alignment, cohesion). Hunt it, lure it, drop objects in its path, and switch to Vectors to see every rule as a coloured force. WebGL 2.

entry.title: Life in Weeks — Knowledge Network
entry.summary: Your life as a grid of weeks: enter a date of birth and see every week lived on a 100- or 120-year calendar, with the world-average life expectancy marked, exact calendar counts and labelled body averages. Nothing leaves your browser.

entry.title: Refraction and total reflection · Reckoning
entry.summary: Snell’s law on an exact ray tracer: refraction into and out of glass, water and diamond, Fresnel reflection, the critical angle and Brewster’s angle.

entry.title: The rainbow · Reckoning
entry.summary: Rays through a drop of water: Descartes’ minimum deviation, the 42° primary bow, the 51° secondary bow and Alexander’s dark band.

entry.title: Prisms and colour · Reckoning
entry.summary: A prism on an exact ray tracer: deviation, minimum deviation, measuring the index, and white light opened into a spectrum.
